arXiv:2410.17276 is **Evaluating Performance and Bias of Negative Sampling in Large-Scale Sequential Recommendation Models**, by **Arushi Prakash, Dimitrios Bermperidis and Srivas Chennu (2024)**. It compares six training negative-sampling strategies using SASRec on MovieLens-10M, Amazon Beauty and RetailRocket, averaging 20 runs. Evaluation ranks the full catalog and stratifies results by target-item training frequency. Aggregate accuracy conceals head/middle/tail disparities: uniform training negatives favor head items; popularity-based sampling can improve balance while reducing overall accuracy. Findings depend on dataset, with explicit caution about RetailRocket variance. This supports popularity-stratified diagnosis, but does not directly establish the effectiveness of frequency-matched evaluation negatives. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.17276v2)

Walid Krichene and Steffen Rendle’s **On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation (KDD 2020)** addresses evaluation sampling: sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; small candidate samples make metrics behave increasingly like AUC. They recommend full-catalog evaluation, or corrections when sampling is necessary. This supplies a measurement warning, not evidence that frequency matching recovers full-catalog HR@10. Frequency-matched candidates should therefore be described as a conditional diagnostic whose validity requires separate evidence. [Research publication](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

For novelty assessment, Prakash et al. already cover popularity-cohort diagnosis and cite closer antecedents: **Dallmann, Zoller and Hotho (2021), A Case Study on Sampling Strategies for Evaluating Neural Sequential Item Recommendation Models**, and **Steck (2011), Item Popularity and Recommendation Accuracy**. A defensible novelty claim would concern the specific frequency-matching procedure and demonstrated diagnostic value, rather than popularity-aware evaluation generally. [Discussion and references](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.17276v2)
